newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end the week down 8.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end the week down 8.3 percent.

text.p: Thai stocks took a beating again on Friday as foreign selling drove the index to finish the week down more than eight percent at a six-year low.

Although some late buying by local funds helped pare losses, the Stock Exchange of Thailand composite index fell 1.41 percent on the day to finish at 605.43 -- the lowest closing level since January 1991.

Heavy foreign selling of finance and bank stocks in the morning took the index down below the key psychological level of 600 points. But local funds bought blue chips shares during the afternoon to bring the market back into the 600-605 range, traders said.
"I think some local funds were coming in as the market is so low and buying back stocks sold earlier in the day. I think the foreigners keep selling," said a broker at Cathay Capital.
Brokers said concerns about the country's economic malaise pulled down share prices.
Thailand's once-robust economy is expected to grow this year by five percent -- a sharp decline for a country which posted average growth of nine percent over the past decade.
Traders also cited worries over the baht currency, high interest rates, sluggish exports and concern over the future of the financial sector.

Currency worries resurfaced at the end of the week following reports that the central bank intervened in the Singapore foreign exchange market on Friday morning after the baht came under speculative attack.
Rumours that a planned merger between Thai Danu Bank Plc and Finance One Plc was in trouble continued to circulate, traders said. Thai Danu denied the talk and said the merger was on track.
Any problems with the merger could cast doubt on others planned in the sector and push one of the government's key economic policies off track, traders said.
The government has encouraged consolidation in the troubled industry, hard-hit by bad loans given to the battered real estate sector.
Communications stocks took another bashing, falling 2.26 percent as first-quarter earnings fears fuelled further sales.
